title: C13 · I wrote the brand rules, then broke them thirteen times
anchor: Brand kit coding system, 5 September 2026; the machine gate that now reads every asset before it is scheduled

slides.headline: I WROTE THE BRAND RULES, THEN BROKE THEM THIRTEEN TIMES
slides.sub: I shipped thirteen assets that broke my own written standard, and I caught none of them by eye.
slides.boundary: Counted across one batch of assets, not a guess.

slides.h2: I WAS THE ONE WHO WROTE IT DOWN
lede: A colour per section, a shape per status, a fixed set of colourways, and a short list of things the copy never does.
Then I produced a run of assets at speed, checked them the way everybody checks their own work, and pushed them out.
slides.boundary: Knowing the rule is not the same as enforcing it.

slides.eyebrow: BREAKS I FOUND ON MY OWN WORK
slides.label: assets out of one batch broke the standard I had written myself, and reviewing them by eye had cleared every one.
slides.sub: Nothing exotic. A wrong ground colour, a banned word in a headline, a punctuation mark the house style does not use.
slides.boundary: Found by a checker, not by looking harder.

slides.h2: WHAT A MACHINE READS BEFORE ANYTHING SHIPS

items.text: No client name anywhere in copy or on a slide
No supplier tied to a named job
No margin, no pay, no money figures
No screenshot of a live book, demo tenant only
Never open on the words everybody opens on
Zero of one punctuation mark the house style does not use

slides.boundary: Six rules, read automatically on every asset and every line of copy.

left.p: You see what you meant to make. Familiarity is the enemy, and you are the most familiar reader you have.

right.p: It has no idea what you meant. It counts, it matches, it fails loudly, and it does not get tired on asset nine.

slides.quote: A standard nobody can check automatically is a preference, and it will be broken by the person who wrote it first.
slides.src: Which is exactly what happened here, thirteen times, in one batch.
slides.boundary: The gate runs before scheduling, not after posting.

lede: Your logo usage guide, your quote template, the rule about how the client name gets spelled. All of it lives in a document somebody read once.
Pick the rule that matters most and make it mechanical. A required field, a checklist that blocks sending, a template that will not let the wrong thing through.
slides.boundary: If it needs somebody to notice, it is already broken somewhere.

lede: Promo shops can request access. The rules that guard the work are part of what I am actually selling.
